scenes.visual: Title card: A Small Difference, a Turn.

scenes.tts: How does a cue only five to ten percent stronger on one side turn a whole axon?
scenes.visual: A growth cone with a pipette at 45 degrees; the near edge shaded slightly darker. Title card: A small difference, a turn.
scenes.narration: How does a cue only five to ten percent stronger on one side turn a whole axon?

scenes.tts: In 1979, Gundersen and Barrett placed a pipette releasing nerve growth factor near chick sensory axons.
scenes.visual: A pipette beside chick sensory axons in a dish. Label: Gundersen and Barrett, 1979; nerve growth factor (NGF).
scenes.narration: In 1979, Gundersen and Barrett placed a pipette releasing nerve growth factor near chick sensory axons.

scenes.tts: Within about twenty minutes, the growth cones turned toward the pipette.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: the growth cone bends toward the pipette. Clock: about 20 minutes.
scenes.narration: Within about twenty minutes, the growth cones turned toward the pipette.

scenes.tts: One growth cone wanders. So the evidence is the spread of turning angles across many cones.
scenes.visual: Many traced paths collapse into a histogram of turning angles, shifted toward the pipette side of zero.
scenes.narration: One growth cone wanders. So the evidence is the spread of turning angles across many cones.

scenes.tts: In a control dish with a uniform bath of cue, the spread centres on zero.
scenes.visual: A second histogram, centred on zero. Label: uniform bath control.
scenes.narration: In a control dish with a uniform bath of cue, the spread centres on zero.

scenes.tts: Now apply the rule to each side. In one common picture, an attractant lets the near side gain more.
scenes.visual: The fan splits into near and far halves, each with added and slides-back bars; the near side's gain is larger. Label: one illustrative mechanism.
scenes.narration: Now apply the rule to each side. In one common picture, an attractant lets the near side gain more.

scenes.tts: It may add actin faster there, ease the backward flow, or engage more clutch. A repellent does the reverse.
scenes.visual: Near side: more actin added, slower flow, more grip. Inset: a repellent shrinks the near side's gain. Label: one illustrative mechanism.
scenes.narration: It may add actin faster there, ease the backward flow, or engage more clutch. A repellent does the reverse.

scenes.tts: The gaining side puts out more filopodia and sheets. The fan shifts that way.
scenes.visual: More filopodia and lamellipodia sprout on the near side; the fan's outline leans toward the pipette.
scenes.narration: The gaining side puts out more filopodia and sheets. The fan shifts that way.

scenes.tts: Microtubules from the centre enter the gaining side more often, and stay longer.
scenes.visual: Green microtubules probe into the near side and stay; fewer enter the far side.
scenes.narration: Microtubules from the centre enter the gaining side more often, and stay longer.

scenes.tts: Behind them the fan narrows, and that stretch becomes axon shaft, pointing the new way.
scenes.visual: The fan narrows behind the microtubules into a new stretch of shaft angled toward the source.
scenes.narration: Behind them the fan narrows, and that stretch becomes axon shaft, pointing the new way.

scenes.tts: Signalling inside the cell can enlarge the small difference. Repeated biased growth then adds up to a turn.
scenes.visual: Several short stretches, each angled slightly more, form a curve. Label: schematic example.
scenes.narration: Signalling inside the cell can enlarge the small difference. Repeated biased growth then adds up to a turn.

scenes.tts: So stabilize the microtubules on one side, with no cue at all. Which way does the growth cone turn?
scenes.visual: A pipette releases a microtubule-stabilizing drug onto one side; no cue present. Question mark.
scenes.narration: So stabilize the microtubules on one side, with no cue at all. Which way does the growth cone turn?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Toward the drug. Buck and Zheng found this in frog spinal neurons.
scenes.visual: The growth cone turns toward the drug. Label: low-dose taxol; Buck and Zheng, 2002, Xenopus spinal neurons.
scenes.caption: Toward the drug. Buck and Zheng found this in frog spinal neurons.
scenes.narration: Toward the drug. Buck and Zheng found this in frog spinal neurons.

scenes.tts: The near side protruded first, and the turn needed actin. Microtubules can start a turn by working through actin.
scenes.visual: The taxol side puts out more lamellipodia before the turn; red actin and green microtubules remodel together. Label: turn needs actin assembly.
scenes.narration: The near side protruded first, and the turn needed actin. Microtubules can start a turn by working through actin.

scenes.tts: Break microtubules down on one side, with a high enough dose, and the cone turns away.
scenes.visual: Nocodazole on one side at an effective dose: microtubules withdraw there and the cone turns away. Small label: a tenfold lower dose gave no turn.
scenes.narration: Break microtubules down on one side, with a high enough dose, and the cone turns away.

scenes.visual: Summary panel: taxol, toward; nocodazole, away.

scenes.tts: Last question. Does the tip need its cell body to decide?
scenes.visual: Zoom out along the long axon to the distant cell body.
scenes.narration: Last question. Does the tip need its cell body to decide?

scenes.tts: In 2001, Campbell and Holt cut frog retinal axons, leaving growth cones with no cell body.
scenes.visual: Scissors cut a retinal axon behind its growth cone. Label: Campbell and Holt, 2001.
scenes.narration: In 2001, Campbell and Holt cut frog retinal axons, leaving growth cones with no cell body.

scenes.tts: The isolated tips still turned in gradients of guidance cues.
scenes.visual: The severed tip turns toward a netrin-1 pipette.
scenes.narration: The isolated tips still turned in gradients of guidance cues.

scenes.tts: In their assay, turning needed protein made from messenger RNA already at the tip.
scenes.visual: Inset: mRNA dots in the tip being translated into protein.
scenes.narration: In their assay, turning needed protein made from messenger RNA already at the tip.

scenes.tts: Not every cue needs new protein. Chick sensory growth cones turned toward nerve growth factor without it.
scenes.visual: Caveat card: depends on the cue and neuron (Roche and colleagues, 2009).
scenes.narration: Not every cue needs new protein. Chick sensory growth cones turned toward nerve growth factor without it.

scenes.tts: So the tip can decide on its own, at least in a dish.
scenes.visual: The severed tip continues on its new heading in the dish.
scenes.narration: So the tip can decide on its own, at least in a dish.

scenes.tts: Carry the rule. A turn sticks where microtubules move in and build axon, and they can start it too.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a turn sticks where microtubules build axon; they can start it too.
scenes.narration: Carry the rule. A turn sticks where microtubules move in and build axon, and they can start it too.

scenes.tts: The cues that make the sides differ, netrins, slits, semaphorins and ephrins, come next.
scenes.visual: Four labelled cue families appear around the growth cone.
scenes.narration: The cues that make the sides differ, netrins, slits, semaphorins and ephrins, come next.

scenes.visual: End card.
